title: Forge 2: a numpy Tensor with broadcasting-aware backward

wrong.no_unbroadcast.py: add's backward passes out.grad straight through, so a broadcast bias keeps the big shape (shape error / wrong gradient)
wrong.mul_no_unbroadcast.py: mul's backward forgets to unbroadcast to each operand's shape
wrong.unbroadcast_leading_only.py: unbroadcast drops leading axes but not size-1 axes ((n,1) columns and (1,m) rows keep the wrong shape)
wrong.matmul_wrong_transpose.py: dB = dC.T @ A instead of A.T @ dC
wrong.sum_no_expand_dims.py: sum(axis=k) backward does not re-insert the reduced axis before broadcasting back
wrong.mean_divides_by_rows.py: mean divides by shape[0] instead of the number of elements averaged
wrong.overwrite_grad.py: tanh backward assigns instead of accumulating (reused tensors lose a path)
wrong.tanh_derivative.py: d tanh is 1 - t instead of 1 - t**2
wrong.pow_exponent.py: d(x**n) is n * x**n instead of n * x**(n-1)
wrong.relu_always_passes.py: relu passes the gradient where the input is negative
wrong.no_seed.py: backward seeds the root with zeros, so every grad stays 0
wrong.no_topo_order.py: backward visits nodes in a plain depth-first order instead of a topological order (diamonds break)

hints: Same recipe as Value: every op returns a new Tensor that remembers its inputs and a _backward closure that ACCUMULATES (+=) into the inputs' grads.

Broadcasting is the new trap: if a (3,) bias was stretched to (5,3) in the forward pass, its gradient is the SUM of the 5 rows. unbroadcast(grad, shape) removes the extra leading axes (sum axis 0) and sums over axes where shape has size 1 (keepdims=True). Call it for every elementwise binary op.
matmul: for C = A @ B, dA = dC @ B.T and dB = A.T @ dC. sum(axis=k) backward must expand_dims back to the reduced axis (unless keepdims) and broadcast_to the input shape; mean is sum times 1/count.
